lines.text: In eighteen ninety-five, engineers built the world's first upside-down roller coaster,
and it nearly snapped riders' necks in half.
See, they designed the loop as a perfect circle.
but created a brutal twelve Gs of force at the bottom.
Riders were blacking out and leaving in ambulances.
So two rival park builders raced to fix it.
One builder grabbed a hammer and bent the track into a tall teardrop,
making the bottom curve wide and gentle.
His rival laughed, calling the skinny loop completely dangerous.
He strapped a wooden test dummy into his own circular loop,
and sent the cart flying down the track.
At the bottom, the dummy was instantly crushed into splinters.
Meanwhile, the teardrop loop worked like magic:
it kept the curve wide where the cart was fast,
and sharp at the top where the cart slowed down.
Which is why today, every looping coaster on Earth uses that bent teardrop,
saving millions of riders from twelve Gs of neck-snapping force.
